title: The diagonal is a regular immersion
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth,
separated, of pure
relative dimension $d$, and put $W=X\times_YX$ with projections
$p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $\Delta:X\hookrightarrow W$. Then $\Delta$
is a regular closed immersion of
pure codimension $d$, and its normal bundle is canonically

$$
N_{\Delta/W}\;\cong\;T_{X/Y}
$$

(the relative tangent bundle of $f$).

proof.text: Since d is positive, use the already proved source-library instance AlgebraicGeometry.isRegularImmersion_diagonal in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.RegularImmersion. It proves the affine-local regularity by the unchanged unit route: standard smooth charts, etale polynomial coordinates, coordinate differences, and restriction to the diagonal. This reuses the normal-form argument already implemented there instead of separately invoking Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleLocalNormalForm.

The product W is locally of finite type over the field, hence locally Noetherian. At each z in X take an affine neighborhood U of Delta(z) and a weakly regular list r of length d generating the diagonal ideal. The stalk is a flat localization of Gamma(W,U), so r remains weakly regular. Since Delta(z) belongs to the zero locus of the diagonal ideal, each generator germ is a nonunit in the local ring. Mathlib IsLocalRing.isRegular_iff_isWeaklyRegular_of_subset_maximalIdeal makes the list regular. The proved closed-immersion identity Scheme.Hom.ker_stalkMap identifies its generated ideal with the kernel of the stalk map.

Apply Mathlib ringKrullDim_add_length_eq_ringKrullDim_of_isRegular to this regular sequence in the Noetherian local stalk. The stalk map of a closed immersion is surjective; RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective identifies the quotient by its kernel with the source stalk. This gives exactly dim O_W,Delta(z) = dim O_X,z + d. Index the regular list by Fin d using List.get and List.ofFn_get; its range is precisely its list membership set, so its ideal is the required span. Combine these two stalk clauses with the given positivity hd.

lean.statement: theorem diagonal_isRegularImmersionOfPureCodimension (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (aY : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [IsSeparated aY] [LocallyOfFiniteType aY] [QuasiCompact aY] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] : IsRegularImmersionOfPureCodimension (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ aY) (pullback.diagonal f) d
lean.note: §1(B): the old upstream isRegularImmersion_diagonal only concludes its affine-local IsRegularImmersion, whose docstring omits the chapter's stalkwise dimension equality; it requires positive codimension. The module states the current blueprint_update using the recorded IsRegularImmersionOfPureCodimension in the fixed separated finite-type field setting, including both stalkwise conditions and the definition's positive-codimension convention. The current blueprint_update removes the historical tangent-bundle conclusion. Rank-zero clopen regularity used by the item is handled directly there, without applying a positive-codimension predicate at zero.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth,
separated, of pure
relative dimension $d$, and put $W=X\times_YX$ with projections
$p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $\Delta:X\hookrightarrow W$. Then $\Delta$
is a regular closed immersion of
pure codimension $d$.

proof.text:
By [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form], $f$ is etale locally the
projection $\mathbf A^d_Y\to Y$; on the model, $\Delta$ is the zero
section of $\mathbf A^d$, a regular closed immersion of codimension
$d$ with normal bundle the trivial rank-$d$ bundle, which under the
identification is $T_{X/Y}$. Regular immersions, their codimension
and their normal bundles are etale local (and compatible with etale
base change), hence the assertion.
